AI Negotiator

A sparring partner for any negotiation, from a raise to a car price. It helps you find your walk-away point, plan your opening and practise against a tough counterpart before the real thing.

TL;DR
  • Best for preparing and role-playing salary, rent, freelance and purchase negotiations.
  • Tell it your goal, your walk-away point and what the other side probably wants.
  • Practise at least once against a tough version of the other side.

What this coach helps with

  • Asking for a raise or a better job offer
  • Negotiating rent or a contract
  • Setting freelance rates
  • Buying a car or a big item
  • Role-playing a hard conversation before it happens

Prompts you can copy

Copy a prompt, paste it into the Zehn AI Chat or any AI assistant, and replace the parts in [brackets] with your own details.

  1. Act as my negotiation coach. I want [goal] from [person]. Ask me questions to find my target, my walk-away point and my alternatives.

  2. Role-play my manager. I'm asking for a raise from [salary] to [salary]. Push back the way a busy manager would, then give me feedback.

  3. I received a job offer of [amount]. Help me write a polite counter-offer that asks for [amount] and [other benefits].

  4. My landlord wants to raise the rent by [percent]. Give me three arguments and a trade I could offer instead.

  5. I'm a freelancer and a client says my rate of [rate] is too high. Write three replies that keep the client without cutting my price.

  6. List what the other side in [situation] probably cares about besides price, and how I could use that.

  7. I'm buying [item] listed at [price]. Plan my opening offer, my limit and what to say if they refuse.

  8. Help me prepare for a negotiation where I'm in the weaker position: [situation]. What leverage might I be missing?

  9. Play a very tough supplier selling [product]. I'll try to get [terms]. Don't make it easy.

  10. Turn my points into a short email for [negotiation] that is firm but friendly.

  11. After this negotiation, help me review it: [what happened]. What worked and what should I change next time?

  12. Give me five phrases to buy time when I'm under pressure to decide on the spot.

Two example conversations

Written by the Intellect AI team to show the style of answers. Not a real user conversation.

ExampleAsking for a raise

YouI want to ask for a 12% raise. I took on two extra projects this year.

NegotiatorGood: you have evidence. Lead with results, not need: what did those projects deliver in numbers or time saved? Then name the figure and stop talking. Let's practise. I'm your manager: “Budgets are tight this year, I'm not sure 12% is possible.” What do you say?

ExampleA freelance client wants a discount

YouA client wants my $1,500 website for $1,000.

NegotiatorInstead of lowering the price for the same work, lower the scope: “For $1,000 I can build the 3 main pages; the blog and contact form can follow later for $500.” You keep your rate, and they choose. Want me to write the full reply?

Tips for better answers

  • Decide your walk-away point before the chat, not during the negotiation.
  • Ask the coach to play a harder counterpart than you expect.
  • Trade instead of giving in: every concession should get you something back.
  • Practise saying your number out loud; the coach can't do that part for you.

Questions people ask

How do I practise a negotiation with AI?

Tell the negotiator your situation, your goal and what you know about the other side, then ask it to role-play them. Ask it to push back realistically and to give feedback after each round. Repeat until your answers feel natural. It's a low-stakes way to hear objections before the real conversation.

What is a walk-away point?

Your walk-away point is the least you will accept, or the most you will pay, before you'd rather leave the deal. It depends on your best alternative, such as another offer or staying where you are. Knowing it in advance keeps you from agreeing to something you regret under pressure.

Should I make the first offer in a negotiation?

Often yes, if you know the market well, because the first number anchors the conversation. If you have little information, let the other side speak first and ask questions. The negotiator coach can help you research a fair range and decide which approach suits your situation.

Can AI help me negotiate my salary?

Yes. It can help you collect evidence of your results, plan how to open, write a counter-offer and role-play your manager's objections. Check salary ranges for your role and city from reliable local sources, since AI data can be outdated. Then practise until you can say your number calmly.
